entry.title: The Capital Kernel — Dykema Gossett as Infrastructure
entry.content:
The Capital Kernel

There is a word for a system that persists across administrations, runs on both parties’ hardware, and provides the formation-compliance layer that all political operations depend on.

That word is operating system.

Dykema Gossett PLLC is Michigan’s political operating system. It runs from 201 Townsend Street, one block from the Capitol. It has been running since at least 1993.

Five Levels, One Firm

No other entity in Michigan occupies this complete vertical:

Level 1: Legislative

Dykema drafted Public Act 362 — the charter school law — in 1993. The law created the authorization framework that allows charter schools to operate outside traditional school board oversight.

Level 2: Judicial

In 1997, when PA 362 was challenged, Dykema defended it at the Michigan Supreme Court. The firm that wrote the law also protected it from constitutional challenge.

Level 3: Authorization

Dykema represents charter authorizers — the entities that grant and renew charter school operating agreements. The firm that wrote the law, defended the law, now represents the entities empowered by the law.

Level 4: Entity Formation

W. Alan Wilk, Dykema’s Team Leader of Political Compliance, has incorporated 7+ dark money vehicles from the firm’s Lansing office. Each one is a 501(c)(4) or LLC registered at or through 201 Townsend Street.

Save Detroit Jobs. Our Neighborhoods First. Detroit Jobs First. RFFW LLC. Put Progress First. Michigan First Principles. Peninsula Fund. All Wilk. All Dykema.

SDJ’s phone number — 517-374-9100 — is Dykema’s switchboard. SDJ’s compliance email is compliance@dykema.com. The IRS filing lists Dykema’s office phone.

Level 5: PAC Compliance

Renae Moore, Dykema’s Senior Compliance Specialist, manages the financial compliance for these vehicles plus the Federal and State PACs. On February 26, 2025, under oath in the Chatfield preliminary examination, she testified to managing 80+ accounts.

80+ accounts. One person. One desk at 201 Townsend.

The Bipartisan Proof

The Federal PAC (FEC C00342113) gave $131,000 to 47 candidates — both parties. The State PAC gave $725,000+ since 2017 — including $13,500 to Duggan and $250 to Yancey.

This is not partisan infrastructure. This is bipartisan infrastructure — and that is what makes it an operating system. It doesn’t care which party is in power. It provides the formation-compliance layer that both parties run on.

The Formation-Compliance Kernel

The kernel has two processes:

Formation (Wilk): Creates legal entities — incorporates 501(c)(4)s, files with LARA, registers agents, establishes bank accounts.

Compliance (Moore): Manages money flows — files FEC reports, files state campaign finance reports, handles IRS 990 filings, testifies when subpoenaed.

Together they form a factory: Wilk produces vehicles, Moore schedules their compliance. The factory runs continuously. The vehicles come and go — SDJ for one election cycle, ONF for another, Peninsula Fund for Chatfield. The factory itself is permanent.

What the Kernel Connects

From 201 Townsend Street, the infrastructure reaches:

DirectionConnectionEvidence
→ BarrettFederal PAC $4,000 FEC C00342113
→ RogersFederal PAC contributionFEC
→ BanksSDJ → $84,000 → Johnson → PCA board IRS 990, TransparencyUSA
→ ChatfieldPeninsula Fund complianceCourt testimony
→ DugganONF formation + State PAC $13,500LARA, TransparencyUSA
→ TremblayProfessional proximity (18yr)Inference, labeled

One address. Six directions. Both parties. Three branches of government.

The Question

An operating system is only visible when it crashes — or when someone reads the source code.

The source code is public. FEC filings. LARA records. IRS 990 data. Court testimony under oath. TransparencyUSA campaign finance records.

Every claim on this page is verifiable. Every link goes to a primary source or a cross-reference within the primals.eco evidence network.

The question is not whether the operating system exists. The question is: who has root access?

entry.title: Dykema Gossett — Michigan's Operating System

Dykema is not a client. Dykema is not a contractor. Dykema is the operating system — the infrastructure layer underneath Michigan politics that persists across administrations, across parties, across decades.

entry.title: Judge Patricia Tremblay — 30th Circuit Court, Ingham County
entry.content:
Judge Patricia Tremblay — 30th Circuit Court

Judge Patricia Tremblay serves on the 30th Circuit Court in Ingham County (Lansing).

She is the judicial node connecting the Dykema capital infrastructure to the Banks charter school enterprise.

The Recusal

Tremblay recused from the Banks PPO case in Ingham County.

The graph records the rationale: proximity to the Dykema/Lansing political compliance world. A 18 -year overlap in Lansing campaign finance makes independence difficult to maintain when the subject’s infrastructure is Dykema’s infrastructure.

Status: The recusal is on the court record. Primary source documentation for the recusal order is being compiled.

Professional Proximity

Two edges connect Tremblay to the Lansing infrastructure cluster:

Dykema Gossett (inference)

  • 18 -year overlap in Lansing campaign finance world
  • Ingham County Bar membership
  • House counsel while Dykema lobbied the legislature
  • Epistemic status: Inference — based on proximity and timing, labeled as such

Aaron Keel (inference)

  • Both served in the House Democratic Caucus
  • Keel was Deputy Chief of Staff
  • Tremblay was Legal Counsel
  • Keel’s revolving door: MASB → House → Treasury → Dykema
  • Epistemic status: Inference — professional co-location, labeled as such

Why This Matters

The Banks enterprise operates across multiple Michigan counties:

  • Wayne County — Purpose Charter Academy, Judge Miller (Board Chair), PPO proceedings
  • Ingham County — Civil action 2026-4349-CZ, Tremblay recusal, Dykema headquarters
  • Oakland County — Additional proceedings

When a judge recuses from a case involving a charter school operator, and that recusal connects to the same law firm infrastructure that formed the dark money vehicle that elected the board member — the graph speaks.

The recusal is proper judicial conduct. What it reveals about the density of connections in the Lansing political compliance world is the finding.

entry.title: Renae Moore — 80 Accounts Under Oath
entry.content:
Renae Moore — The Compliance Scheduler

Renae Moore is a Senior Compliance Specialist at Dykema Gossett PLLC, 201 Townsend Street, Lansing.

  • Phone: 517-374-9121
  • Email: rmoore@dykema.com

If Wilk builds the vehicles, Moore drives all of them at once.

February 26, 2025 — Under Oath

On February 26, 2025, Renae Moore took the witness stand in Ingham County District Court. She was the first witness called in the preliminary examination of former Michigan House Speaker Lee Chatfield, who faces 13 felony charges including embezzlement and conspiracy.

Under oath, she testified to three things:

  1. She manages the compliance for 80+ accounts — dark money vehicles, PACs, campaign committees
  2. She had no duty to report how money was spent (including strip-club expenses)
  3. The Peninsula Fund had compliance issues she was aware of

Six Simultaneous Roles

EntityMoore’s RoleStatus
Save Detroit JobsAssistant SecretaryActive
Our Neighborhoods FirstComplianceActive
Detroit Jobs FirstComplianceActive
RFFW LLCTreasurer$1M complaint
Peninsula FundComplianceDefendant (Chatfield charges)
Promise to the People FundComplianceAG-affiliated

The dual role on the last two is the finding:

  • Peninsula Fund: Chatfield’s dark money vehicle, subject of the prosecution
  • Promise to the People Fund: Affiliated with the Attorney General’s office — the entity prosecuting Chatfield

Moore simultaneously serves the defendant and the prosecutor’s affiliated fund. One compliance specialist. Both sides.

What 80 Accounts Means

80+ accounts is not a number. It is a capacity. One person cannot meaningfully monitor compliance across 80+ dark money flows. What Moore provides is not oversight — it is compliance theater.

The accounts share:

  • One compliance specialist (Moore)
  • One formation attorney (Wilk)
  • One law firm address (201 Townsend)
  • One phone number ( 517-374-9100 )

This is not a compliance department. It is a scheduling problem.

entry.title: Tom Barrett — U.S. House MI-7
entry.content:
Tom Barrett — U.S. House MI-7

Tom Barrett is the U.S. Representative for Michigan’s 7th Congressional District, based in Charlotte. Former State Senator. Army veteran. On the ballot November 3, 2026.

Barrett’s campaign infrastructure connects directly to the Dykema Gossett capital kernel at 201 Townsend Street.

Dykema Money

Dykema Gossett Federal PAC (FEC C00342113) contributed $4,000 to Barrett’s campaign.

The same PAC gave to 47 candidates in both parties — $131,000 total. The same law firm formed Save Detroit Jobs, whose $84,000 expenditure elected the council member who now sits on the board of a charter school run by a man with 9 criminal convictions.

Barrett’s $4,000 from Dykema PAC is not large. What matters is what it connects to: the entire dark money formation apparatus at 201 Townsend Street.

Outside Money

SourceAmount% of OutsideType
AFP Action $477,780 44.8% Independent expenditure
NRCC $6,300,000 —Party committee spend in MI-7
Kenneth Griffin (Citadel) $7,000 —Individual donation
Stephen Schwarzman (Blackstone)Maxed—Individual donation

Griffin and Schwarzman are cross-ticket donors — they fund both Barrett and Mike Rogers (Senate). Same money, same infrastructure, different branches of the same tree.

The “Convicted Felon” Projection

On August 13, 2026, Barrett called his opponent William Lawrence a “convicted felon.”

Lawrence’s conviction: a 2013 pipeline protest arrest. The conviction was expunged under Michigan’s Clean Slate Act (MCL 780.623). It does not exist in the legal record.

Meanwhile, Barrett’s PAC donor infrastructure includes:

  • Kenneth Daniels — SDJ president, federal felon ( $21M drug ring, DEA May 12, 2014)
  • Brian Banks — 9 criminal convictions (6 felony, 3 misdemeanor) , connected via shared Dykema infrastructure

Barrett called the water protector a felon. His own infrastructure tree is rooted in actual felons.

Jason Roe — Senior Advisor

Jason Roe of Roe Strategic LLC served as Barrett’s senior advisor. FEC records show $114,000+ in consulting fees.

Roe is connected to the wrong election date incident: an ad in a Black newspaper (Michigan Bulletin) listed the election as November 6 instead of November 5. The City Pulse ran the correct date. The Michigan Attorney General issued a cease-and-desist.
